items.basis: Műszakpótlék, Mt. 141 §: 30% of the hourly base wage for work between 18:00 and 06:00 in multi-shift work where the daily start time varies (on ≥ 1/3 of working days, ≥ 4 h between earliest and latest start) — met by rotating 3 × 8 h

items.value: Betegszabadság: up to 15 working days a year paid by the employer at 70% of absence pay (távolléti díj); sickness benefit (táppénz) from the social insurer thereafter

items.basis: ASSUMPTION (not sourced): 10 working days of sickness a year, all inside the 15-day employer-paid betegszabadság

Fully-loaded hourly cost INCLUDES: KSH total gross earnings (base + bonuses / premiums + allowances, as KSH measures them) for the occupation, 2025 national average indexed +8.4% to 2026 and scaled ×0.9406 to the four clusters; paid annual leave (27 days) and weekday public holidays inside the 12 monthly salaries; employer-paid sick leave at 70% for 10 days; the 30% shift allowance (Mt. 141) on the 50% of hours that fall 18:00–06:00 in rotating 3 × 8 h (shop-floor roles), carried into leave and sick pay; szocho 13% on all of it; divided by 1728 productive hours.

NOT included (not shown to be standard by a source, or not verified): 13th-month salary (not statutory in Hungary; any annual bonus is already inside KSH total earnings); cafeteria / SZÉP-card benefits (common but not statutory; their tax would add on top); commuting reimbursement (statutory share of pass / ticket cost, Korm. rendelet 39/2010 — not verified); rehabilitation contribution for employers ≥ 25 staff short of the 5% disabled-employee quota (not verified); work clothing, occupational medicine, training time; overtime, weekend and holiday premiums; child additional leave; agency margins; the vocational-training contribution (believed abolished 2022).
items.notes: Overlap: KSH occupation averages include the shift allowances already paid to shift workers, so adding the full allowance may overstate shop-floor rates by up to ~12%; the rate without the allowance is printed in each basis.
